I1.quote: Searched main text and SI for a gravimetric, volumetric (Sieverts) or flow measurement of H2 uptake by a sorbent (isotherm, mass gain, pressure drop, flow rate). None found. Uptake is shown only by ESI-MS of a CH2Cl2 solution: "ESI-MS shows uptake of 2 H2 to give [Rh6(PCy3)6H16][BArF4]2 B." The "0.1 % w/w" capacity is attributed to cluster mass, not to a measured uptake.

I5.quote: Hydrogen storage is an area of intense current interest, which is driven by the requirements for reversible storage of dihydrogen for future energy applications.

notes: Molecular Rh6 phosphine hydride cluster ([Rh6(PCy3)6H12][BArF4]2) taking up 2 H2 per cluster in CH2Cl2 solution (SI, 'Procedure for the storage / release cycle', SI p. 3: H2 admitted at 77 K then warmed to 298 K, ~4 atm), followed by ESI-MS, NMR, EPR, cyclic voltammetry and DFT. No carbon sorbent, no surface area, no uptake isotherm. I1 fails on method (ESI-MS stoichiometry is not gravimetric, volumetric or flow), so I2 to I4 not assessed. Not coded theoretical_only (experimental work present). Not coded electrochemical: the H2 is taken up by gas addition to a solution, and the cyclic voltammetry (CH2Cl2, [NBu4][BArF4], glassy carbon electrode) probes the metal-cluster redox couples that trigger H2 release; judged a reaction of hydrogen without a measured uptake, hence no_conditions_stated. A reader taking the redox-triggered electrochemical release in electrolyte as 'electrochemistry of hydrogen' would code electrochemical instead; either way the paper is excluded. Not retracted (record is_retracted false). Original data, not a review. No statement that all H2 values were published before (ref. 21 is cited only for B retaining H2 for weeks).
